title: Ed May's decision augmentation theory

tellings.quote: decision augmentation uh that pre pre the the researchers precognition is drawing them to start an experiment

plain: The parapsychology researcher Ed May proposed that when psychic experiments seem to work, it may be because the researchers' own precognition, a sense of the future, leads them to start each experiment at just the right moment. The writer Eric Wargo describes this idea, which May called "decision augmentation", to Michels. If it is right, the strange results in such studies would come from foreknowledge guiding the people involved, not from anyone moving matter with their mind.
